reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows N-doping forms M–N bonds, enhances corrosion resistance, and improves stability in a Pt-based HEA fuel-cell catalyst, but it does not address automotive exhaust conditions (H2O, NO, thermal aging) or low-PGM, nearly equiatomic alloys for that application, leaving the transferability premise unsupported.
premises: N-doping forms stable metal–nitrogen bonds in multi-element alloys
M–N bonds suppress metal leaching and corrosion
M–N bonds tune electronic structure and adsorption energetics
N-doping improves catalytic stability under harsh conditions
These effects are transferable from fuel-cell HEA catalysts to automotive exhaust catalysts
